html:
The world order is today dominated by an escalating confrontation between the US and Iran, marked by explicit threats from Trump and Iran's claims of an impending renewed US bombing campaign, alongside its conditions for ending the conflict and reopening a critical oil transit route.

US-Iran Tensions: Tensions in the Middle East are rapidly escalating, with Iran claiming the US is planning to renew a bombing campaign against the Islamic Republic and has raised its military preparedness to the highest level. Trump stated he is considering "wiping Iran out" and questioned "If and when do I blow the entire nation up?" while cutting short a visit to Camp David. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf declared that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's conditions are met, and Iran has conveyed these terms to the US for both reopening the Strait and ending the war. The US is warning of rapid escalation in the Middle East, with oil prices surpassing $100 per barrel amidst the regional instability.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: Ukraine launched its "largest ever" drone attack on Moscow, with the mayor reporting 450 drones downed, causing two deaths and damage to an oil refinery and residential building. Ukrainian officials state over 1,000 drones were fired at Russia. Despite the attacks, Russia's ruling United Russia party is projected to win tightly controlled parliamentary elections, which for the first time include votes in regions Moscow illegally annexed from Ukraine. Meanwhile, France, Poland, and other European allies are alarmed by escalating Russian "hybrid" attacks.

European Political Shifts: German Chancellor Merz described state election losses for his CDU party in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern as a "disaster," with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) making significant gains. Merz has vowed to stay in office and press ahead with economic reforms despite the setback. In parallel, French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met to strengthen bilateral ties and develop shared space launch infrastructure, with both leaders noting increasingly awkward relations with the US. A UK minister warned that Trump’s Iran war will impact next month’s budget as Prime Minister Burnham prepares to meet Trump.

Middle East Security: Saudi Arabia reported shooting down a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, attributed to Houthi rebels, who claim to have targeted the capital with missiles and sensitive sites at Riyadh airport and Aramco in Yanbu. Jordan and the UN Security Council condemned the Houthi attacks. Concurrently, a suspected Palestinian gunman killed an Israeli man in the West Bank, identified as Natanel Kron, while Israeli soldiers killed a Palestinian motorist whom the military said was attempting to run them over. These incidents occur on the eve of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, as the US approved the sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia.

Other Global Developments: Beyond the immediate conflicts, more than a dozen people have been arrested in connection with the 2021 assassination of Haitian president Jovenel Moïse. In Pakistan, Aleema Khanum, the sister of ex-PM Imran Khan, was arrested on accusations of mobilizing supporters for country-wide protests. The cultural sphere saw Ed Sheeran admit "mistakes" after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks, leading to protests and a matching $1 million donation from Ms Rachel for Palestinian children. Italy's Meloni announced plans to ban veils in schools and limit foreign students per class.
